note: Hand-written, hand-labeled transcripts written before the extractor existed, but the extractor's rules were then designed while reading them, so this is a development set, not a held-out one. See blind-set.json for held-out numbers.

meetings.title: Checkout reliability sync
meetings.transcript:
Priya: Okay, let's get started. Can everyone hear me?
Marcus: Yep.
Priya: So first thing, the checkout latency spike from Thursday. Jun, where are we?
Jun: Um, so we traced it to the connection pool on the payments service. I already bumped the pool size on Friday, so it's stable for now.
Priya: Great. Do we need a proper fix?
Jun: Yeah. I'll write up the postmortem by Wednesday and I'll add an alert on pool saturation.
Marcus: I can take a look at why the pool was exhausted in the first place, I have a hunch it's the retry storm.
Priya: Please do. Elena, could you add a regression test for the timeout path before the release?
Elena: Sure, I'll have it in by Thursday.
Priya: Perfect. Second topic, the release date. We talked about pushing to the 14th.
Marcus: Honestly I think we should just go with the 14th, the migration isn't done.
Priya: Okay, decision: we ship on October 14th instead of the 9th.
Elena: That works for QA.
Marcus: I'm blocked on the schema migration until the DBA team approves the change window.
Priya: I'll ping the DBA lead today.
Jun: Oh and someone should probably update the on-call runbook at some point.
Priya: Yeah. Let's not lose that. Marcus, can you own the runbook update?
Marcus: Hmm, not this week, I'm buried in the migration. Maybe next sprint.
Elena: I can do it if nobody else has time.
Priya: Thanks Elena. Anything else? No? Great, thanks all.

actions.action: add an alert on pool saturation
look at why the pool was exhausted
add a regression test for the timeout path

meetings.title: Q4 planning - growth
meetings.transcript:
Fatima: Thanks for joining. Goal today is to lock the Q4 bets.
Aisha: Before we start, I pulled the funnel numbers. Activation dropped about 4% after the onboarding change.
Fatima: Hm, that's not great. Can you break it down by platform? Ideally before Friday's review.
Aisha: Yeah, can do.
Tom: I suspect it's the new permissions screen on Android. I'll dig into the session recordings when I get a chance.
Sai: From the eng side, the permissions screen is easy to revert if we need to.
Fatima: Let's not revert yet. We agreed we'd wait for Aisha's breakdown first.
Fatima: Okay, Q4 bets. I'm proposing three: referral program, faster checkout, and the Android redesign.
Tom: The redesign is huge. I don't think we can do it this quarter.
Sai: Agreed, it's at least two quarters of eng work.
Fatima: Fine, we're going with referrals and checkout for Q4, redesign moves to Q1.
Fatima: Sai, I need a rough estimate for the referral program by next Tuesday.
Sai: Sure. I'll pair with Tom on it.
Tom: I'll put together some referral flow mocks for Sai by Monday.
Aisha: I won't be able to support the referral analytics until November, just flagging.
Fatima: Noted. We're waiting on legal to sign off on the referral terms anyway.
Fatima: I'll chase legal tomorrow.
Sai: Maybe I should also look at the checkout payment SDK upgrade, it's been on my list forever.
Fatima: Please. Okay that's time, thanks everyone.

actions.action: rough estimate for the referral program
look at the checkout payment SDK upgrade

meetings.title: Platform weekly
meetings.transcript:
Priya: Quick one today. Status on last week's items?
Jun: Postmortem is published, I sent it out yesterday. The pool saturation alert is still on my list.
Elena: Regression test for the timeout path is merged.
Marcus: Still blocked on the DBA approval, honestly.
Priya: Ugh. I'll escalate it to their director today.
Jun: I'll get the alert done by end of week, promise.
Marcus: Also, I looked at the retry storm thing. It's the client SDK retrying without backoff.
Priya: Can we fix that on our side?
Marcus: Partially. I could add a server-side rate limit, but the real fix is in the SDK.
Priya: Okay. Let's do both. Marcus, you own the rate limit, and Elena, can you file a ticket with the SDK team?
Elena: Will do, I'll file it this afternoon.
Marcus: Fine, rate limit by next Friday.
Jun: Should we also tell support about the SDK issue?
Priya: Good call. Let me think about who should own comms.
Priya: Decision for the record: no client SDK changes until the vendor responds.
Jun: Got it. That's it from me.

actions.action: escalate DBA approval to their director
file a ticket with the SDK team
figure out who should own comms
